reasoning: A maximal trail begun at any vertex cannot stop at a different vertex: at a noninitial endpoint the used incident-edge count is odd, while total degree is even, so an unused incident edge remains. Thus it is closed. Removing its edges leaves even residual degrees because a closed trail uses an even number of incident edges at each vertex. Every nonempty residual edge-component meets the initial closed trail by connectedness of the original graph. Inductively find an Euler closed trail in each residual component and splice all of them into the initial trail at shared vertices.
